clue.text: Insect head and wing

blocks.note: the head on a glass of beer is its froth
a fly is a flap or wing, as in a tent's fly or the flies above a stage

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes two parts of some creature's body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' and 'wing' look like body parts of the insect, but each is a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: The frothfly, or froghopper, is a small bug whose larvae hide inside a blob of spittle-like foam on plants.

clue.text: Truly local fruit — one being English

indicators.note: being means becoming instead, so one letter turns into another

blocks.note: figs are a fruit
I is the Roman numeral one
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Genuinely home-grown produce, one item English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word: fegs is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Fegs is a Scots exclamation meaning in faith, used as an oath like indeed or truly.

clue.text: Be able to manage number going around tense after game

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so these letters wrap the next one

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
No is the abbreviation for number
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Coping with the numbers in a tense match.
explanation.definitionFit: To run to something is to afford it or stretch that far, as in a budget that won't run to a holiday.

clue.text: Model T they alter as lead compound is in fuel

definitions.note: the answer is the first word of the compound's name, tetraethyl lead

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters are reformed

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Car owners tinker with an old Ford as fuel changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model T' looks like the Ford car; Model is the anagram signal and T is fodder. The second anagram-sounding word, alter, is simply fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetraethyl lead was the antiknock additive once put in petrol, so tetraethyl names that compound.

clue.text: Sacked absent politician? Mine might have a problem with that

definitions.text: Mine might have a problem with that
definitions.note: a cryptic description, a noun phrase

blocks.note: sacked means dismissed from a job
A is the abbreviation for absent
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A sacked politician who never turns up could cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as the possessive, as though someone has a gripe; it is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is explosive methane that collects in coal mines, a long-standing danger to miners.

clue.text: Old river sediment spades removed

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so that letter goes

blocks.note: lees are the dregs at the bottom of wine
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Silt is dredged out of an ancient waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee was formerly a word for a stream or river, and the Lee is also a river in Ireland.

clue.text: Gossip craving thanks

blocks.note: a yen is a longing
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A busybody eager to be thanked.
explanation.definitionFit: A yenta is a Yiddish term for a meddlesome woman who chatters about other people's business.

clue.text: Refuse cataloguing system for books

blocks.note: first meaning: the skins and pips left after grapes or apples are pressed
second meaning: the Machine-Readable Cataloguing standard used by libraries

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, as if a library turns books away, but it is the noun meaning waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the pressed residue of fruit in winemaking, and MARC is the library record format for catalogue data.

clue.text: Look into a principle without support

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the first word is put within the second

blocks.note: a cause is a principle one stands for
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Examining a philosophy that has no backing.
explanation.walkthrough: LO goes inside A CAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acaulose plants are stemless, lacking the stalk that would otherwise hold them up.

clue.text: Those involved in racket reported traveller lad

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the clue words are heard rather than read

blocks.note: a Rom is a Romany traveller and a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Members of a gang have been named as involved in a crooked scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests crime; it is noise. 'Traveller' is the British term for Romany and other itinerant people.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhomboi are bullroarers, slats whirled on a cord in ancient rites to make a roaring din.

clue.text: Type of bread Italian company felt advanced

blocks.note: Cia is the Italian abbreviation for compagnia, company
batt is a sheet of felted wadding
A is the abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: An Italian bakery firm decides to move up its plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' looks like a verb, as in what the company thought; it is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciabatta is a flat, open-textured white loaf that originated in Italy.

clue.text: Obliging spirit of Brussels girl?

blocks.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
a genie is a spirit that grants its master's wishes

explanation.surface: A helpful ghost haunting a young Belgian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is only an example: the answer is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugenie is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl by way of example.

clue.text: Wise Man without a bit of myrrh or gold representative of another land

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letters are taken away from the name

blocks.note: Melchior is traditionally one of the three Magi
the first letter of myrrh
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: One of the Magi arrives at the stable missing some of his gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Melchior loses his M and his OR, leaving ELCHI.
explanation.definitionFit: An elchi is an ambassador, an envoy sent to act for a foreign ruler, in old Turkish and Persian usage.

clue.text: Gannet flying about with river bird

indicators.note: things flying are tossed about through the air, so the letters of gannet land in a new order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the others

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
W is the abbreviation for with
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A seabird flies over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnatwren is a tiny long-billed songbird of tropical America, related to the gnatcatchers.

clue.text: Horse cloth, it covers middle of the pair carrying queen

indicators.note: middle of points to the central letter of the following word
covers means lies over and around, so these letters enclose the next
carrying means holding within, so the word for the pair takes the queen inside

blocks.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
the central letter of the
a brace is a pair, as of game birds
Qu is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A saddlecloth draped over two horses with a queen riding.
explanation.walkthrough: It, in crosswords, is often sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shabracque is a cavalry saddlecloth, the decorated cloth laid over a horse under the saddle.

clue.text: Grower’s skill entering them half cut in local prize stupefied

indicators.note: half cut means half of the word is chopped off, here its second half
entering means going inside, so these letters are placed within the others

blocks.note: gree is a Scots word for a prize or the victory
stupefied, deadened in feeling
taken as written, before its back half goes

explanation.surface: Drunk gardeners are left dazed after winning at a village show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' is British slang for drunk, which is the picture; here it trims a word. 'Local' flags dialect: GREE is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a green thumb is an idiom for a natural talent for making plants flourish.

clue.text: Core community’s fine for fifty

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands in where the other was

blocks.note: local means belonging to a community
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood group is fined fifty pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCAL swaps its first L for F.
explanation.definitionFit: Focal means central or of chief importance, as a core issue is a central one.

clue.text: Surpassing a jewel, one stolen in French society

indicators.note: stolen means taken away, so the one is removed from the jewel
in means placed inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: a bijou is a jewel or trinket
I is the Roman numeral one
Fr is the abbreviation for French
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A gem is stolen from a high-society Parisian gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: A BIJOU loses its I, then sits between FR and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Frabjous, Lewis Carroll's coinage in Jabberwocky, means wonderful or splendid, beyond the ordinary.

clue.text: Wild centaury which might be poisonous

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the plant's letters run free into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written: centaury is a wild flower

explanation.surface: A wild flower that might be toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' sits naturally before a plant name, so it hides its job as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyanuret is an old name for a cyanide, a class of compounds many of which are lethal poisons.

clue.text: Very pointed rule by supreme commander in hall

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the commander goes within the word for hall

blocks.note: an aula is a hall
CIC is commander-in-chief
R is an abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: A commander-in-chief lays down strict orders in the great hall.
explanation.walkthrough: CIC, short for commander-in-chief, is standard military shorthand; aula is Latin for a hall, used of university halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Acicular means needle-shaped, slender and sharply tipped, as some crystals and leaves are.

clue.text: Dirty old skate

definitions.note: a verb, to dirty, in an obsolete sense

blocks.note: first meaning: an obsolete verb meaning to defile or soil
second meaning: a flat cartilaginous fish

explanation.surface: A grubby elderly skater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' tells you the first sense is archaic; it does not describe the skate.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish called a skate is a kind of ray, and ray was once also a verb meaning to befoul.

clue.text: Mountainous land even if worthless in the Highlands

blocks.note: and is an archaic conjunction meaning if or even if
orra is Scots for odd or worthless

explanation.surface: Even barren country is still valued in the Scottish hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highlands are the Scottish mountain region, so ORRA is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small principality set high in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

clue.text: Military rule rose before Wellington perhaps

blocks.note: jack is short for the Jacqueminot, a deep red rose
a wellington is a kind of rubber boot

explanation.surface: A floral tribute to the Duke of Wellington.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington looks like the general, which suits the military theme, but here he is a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackboot stands figuratively for oppressive, authoritarian government enforced by soldiers.

clue.text: Corporal, one picking up speaker at defence meeting?

blocks.note: one means a single, the article a
the North Atlantic Treaty Organization is a defence alliance
a mic picks up whoever is speaking

explanation.surface: A soldier with a microphone eavesdrops at a military conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporal' looks like a rank but is the adjective. The wordplay is a whole picture: a NATO mic, the microphone at an alliance meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal means relating to the body, which is what anatomic describes in its structural sense.

clue.text: Press time cut by hour

indicators.note: cut by means reduced by, so the following letter is taken out

blocks.note: sith is an obsolete word for time or occasion
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A newspaper's deadline is brought forward an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press time' reads as one phrase, a newspaper's deadline, but splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit can mean to press or weigh down, as a burden sits heavily on someone.

clue.text: Particle involving zero spin

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so these letters enclose the zero

blocks.note: the word spin, which also signals its own rearrangement
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A physics note that a particle has zero spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' is both fodder and its own anagram signal: spun, it becomes PSIN, round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A psion is a psi meson, a subatomic particle made of a charm quark and its antiquark.

clue.text: Heroin from the US with Ecstasy in pouches

indicators.note: with here means holding, so the drug word has the other letter inside it

blocks.note: caca is American slang for heroin
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Smuggled drugs are hidden in bags.
explanation.walkthrough: E sits in the middle of CACA.
explanation.definitionFit: Caeca are blind-ended pouches of the gut, such as the one at the start of the large intestine.

clue.text: Dog perhaps dropping a part of jellyfish

indicators.note: dropping means falling lower, and in this down entry the letter a falls to the bottom

blocks.note: a canid is any member of the dog family

explanation.surface: A dog lets go of part of a jellyfish it found on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The A moves from second place down to the foot of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cnida is a nematocyst, one of the stinging cells a jellyfish fires at prey.

clue.text: Rapture you can develop with Jesu

indicators.note: to develop is to grow into a different form, so the letters reshape themselves

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A promise of religious ecstasy through faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring' is the tune the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Jouysaunce is Spenser's word for joyfulness or delight, close to rapture in meaning.

clue.text: Plans to spend a day in Rome

indicators.note: to spend is to use up, so that letter is gone

blocks.note: ideas are plans
taken as written

explanation.surface: Holiday plans for a day of sightseeing in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient Roman calendar the ides fell on the 13th or 15th of each month.

clue.text: With little ready I will certainly get something to chew

blocks.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
I is an old spelling of ay, meaning yes, certainly
a quid is a lump of tobacco for chewing

explanation.surface: A man short of money vows to buy some chewing tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is British slang for cash, as in the readies.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiquid describes someone whose assets cannot easily become money, hence short of spare cash.

clue.text: Feature of Early English branch line

indicators.note: a feature of something is a part of it, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Architecture talk: a detail of Early English style, the Gothic period.
explanation.walkthrough: Early English is the first phase of English Gothic church building.
explanation.definitionFit: A lye is a short railway siding or branch track off the main line.

clue.text: Rust — treat after earlier operation

indicators.note: after means following, so the word for treat is placed second, behind the other piece

blocks.note: ure is an obsolete word for use or operation
a do is a party or treat

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a patient after an earlier surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier' marks URE as an old word, not a sequence of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is the name for the rust fungi and the summer spore stage that gives plants rusty blotches.

clue.text: Synagogue regularly plundered in the middle city

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
in the middle points to the central letters of the word that comes before

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
the central three letters

explanation.surface: A synagogue looted in the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is a real city, the capital of Cameroon in West Central Africa.

clue.text: Hindu custom turning back palms

indicators.note: turning back means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: the ita is a South American palm tree

explanation.surface: A ritual of turning one's palms away.

clue.text: Potential killer close to US city? One must leave

indicators.note: must leave means has to go, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: near Las Vegas, the Nevada city
A stands for one

explanation.surface: A murderer is lurking on the outskirts of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAR VEGAS loses an A.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve agent is a chemical weapon that attacks the nervous system and can kill.
